title: `certified` is a hardcoded `true` at four call sites for the ONE connector this platform has, whose provider review is `NOT_SUBMITTED` — the Connection Center says "connected and working" about a capability /api/ai/chat refuses to use
why_open: `resolveCapability` (apps/web/src/lib/connections/capability-resolution.ts:73) does refuse a connect action when `certified` is false, and it has real callers — but nothing DERIVES `certified`. It is written as the literal `certified: true` at apps/web/src/app/(app)/settings/page.tsx:57, :69, :81 and apps/web/src/components/ai/TenureAIPanel.tsx:308. For `ai.model` that literal is false: packages/platform-config/src/provider-review.ts:207 records `RELAY_ANTHROPIC_REVIEW.state = "NOT_SUBMITTED"` with `approvedScopes: []`, and apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:299-316 calls `providerActivation(RELAY_ANTHROPIC_SCOPES, RELAY_ANTHROPIC_REVIEW)` and refuses every vendor call because of it. So with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set, `aiConfigured()` is true, `configured: aiConfigured()` is true, `certified: true` is asserted, and `resolveCapability` returns CONNECTED with the sentence "Tenure AI model is connected and working." — for a connector the request path will not call. That is exactly the working-looking-but-uncertified surface WRK-030-005 forbids, and the untruthfulness half of WRK-GATE-110. Separately, `cellLoginMethods` (apps/web/src/lib/auth-connections.ts:124) and `connectionRefusals` (:135) were written to answer "which sign-in methods may be drawn" and "why is a configured connection not offered" and have ZERO production callers — the only importer of that file is `auth.ts:15`, which takes `oktaIsUsable` alone; apps/web/src/app/signin/page.tsx:24 decides what to render from the raw `process.env.AUTH_DEV_LOGIN` string and never consults the registry.
smallest_real_change: Add a single exported resolver in apps/web/src/lib/connections/capability-resolution.ts — e.g. `certifiedCapabilityState(key)` — that computes `certified` from `providerActivation(RELAY_ANTHROPIC_SCOPES, RELAY_ANTHROPIC_REVIEW)` (already exported from @tenure/platform-config, already imported by chat/route.ts, so cell-independence holds) instead of a literal, and have settings/page.tsx and TenureAIPanel.tsx call it rather than writing `certified:` inline. With the review at NOT_SUBMITTED, `ai.model` resolves to NOT_CERTIFIED, the settings card loses its "connected and working" sentence, and the Relay panel's card stops offering a path that cannot work. Then add a lexical guard under tests/architecture that fails if `certified:` appears as a literal `true`/`false` in any `.tsx` under apps/web/src/app or apps/web/src/components, so the next surface cannot re-derive it wrong. Prove it by mutating `RELAY_ANTHROPIC_REVIEW.state` to `"APPROVED"` and asserting the settings test flips CONNECTED↔NOT_CERTIFIED — i.e. assert on what the PAGE emits, not on `resolveCapability` called directly. Also give `cellLoginMethods`/`connectionRefusals` their caller: signin/page.tsx renders methods from `cellLoginMethods()` and, for an operator, the refusal reasons — or delete them as dead code. Do not touch apps/system-studio.

title: There is no `MemoryCandidate` anywhere in the tree; a machine writes org-wide memory with no review, and `MemoryRecord.sensitivity` is read by nothing on any memory path
why_open: `MemoryCandidate` appears in exactly one place in the repository — the ledger line docs/implementation/universal-work-graph-execution-ledger.md:539 — and in no schema, package or module. Meanwhile the review-free path already runs: apps/web/src/lib/outbox/consumers.ts:90 has the `ApprovalDecided` consumer `tx.memoryRecord.create({...})` with `roleId` unset and `sensitivity` unset, so every approval decision (finance, HR, anything) becomes an ORG-WIDE, `standard`-classified knowledge card that every club member sees, written by software with no human or policy review — the exact opposite of Bible §9.5 ("Human/policy review decides whether it becomes … a restricted tenant record … an ephemeral personal note; rejected/no retention"). The private-vs-role separation is equally absent: `canSeeMemoryCard` (apps/web/src/lib/memory.ts:10-13) takes `card: { roleId: string | null }` and never looks at `sensitivity`, which has existed on the model since the baseline (apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma:792). Documents ARE clearance-gated on the identical code path — apps/web/src/lib/search-data.ts:78-84 selects `sensitivity` and passes it to `authorizeRetrieved` — while the memory query two statements above it, search-data.ts:70-73, selects `{ id, title, content, roleId, organizationId }` and no `sensitivity`, so a `restricted` card is authorized by org-visibility alone. apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[slug]/memory/page.tsx:57-63 has the same hole. And `MemoryRecordType.CREDENTIAL` at schema.prisma:776 carries the comment "Login / access info — stored encrypted" while nothing in apps/web encrypts anything (`grep -rn encrypt apps/web/src` returns exactly one hit, `ServerSideEncryption: "AES256"` in s3.ts:132) — so the one card type explicitly meant to hold secrets is stored as plaintext JSON by createMemoryCard (memory/actions.ts:37-49) at the default clearance.
smallest_real_change: Two halves, neither needing a schema change. (1) Separation: widen `canSeeMemoryCard`'s card parameter to `{ roleId: string | null; sensitivity?: string | null }` and gate it through the existing `sensitivityRank`/clearance ladder in apps/web/src/lib/search.ts, then fix BOTH construction sites — add `sensitivity: true` to the memory `select` in search-data.ts:72 and pass it into the call at :117, and let memory/page.tsx:57's `findMany` carry it (it uses `include`, so it already has the column). Grep confirms those are the only two callers of `canSeeMemoryCard`. (2) Governed review: give the machine writer a candidate step rather than a direct write — in outbox/consumers.ts, classify the decision through a new pure `memoryCandidateVerdict()` in memory.ts implementing Bible §9.5's five outcomes, and write the resulting record role-scoped (`roleId` = the approving seat) and `sensitivity: "restricted"` for finance/HR approval types instead of org-wide/standard. Also fix the false claim at schema.prisma:776 — either encrypt CREDENTIAL content or change the comment (fix the CLAIM, not the test). Mutation to prove it: set the memory row's `sensitivity` to `restricted` in the itest fixture and assert an ordinary member's corpus does NOT contain it, then revert the `select` change and confirm the itest goes red. NOTE: a full `MemoryCandidate` review QUEUE (a pending row a person approves) needs a new model in apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma + a migration — if the implementer takes that, it must be stated, since another run may be writing that file.

title: `findSecretValues` has exactly ONE production caller (the outbox); the model-prompt, log, config and evidence sinks the requirement names are unguarded, and no test proves any of the six
why_open: The requirement is "Prove browser/model/log/event/config/evidence never receive reusable provider secrets" — six sinks, and the operative word is Prove. Two are genuinely covered: browser by tests/security/no-tokens-in-browser-storage.test.mjs, and event by apps/web/src/lib/outbox/outbox.ts:113, which is the ONLY production call to `findSecretValues` in the whole tree (grep across apps/packages/tests/modules returns that line plus the re-exports at packages/audit/src/index.ts:61-65). Audit metadata is redacted by value at packages/audit/src/record.ts:350. The other three named sinks have nothing. **model**: apps/web/src/lib/ai.ts:101-118 builds the vendor body from `system`+`user` and posts it to api.anthropic.com with no value scan; apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:334-355 hands it retrieved tenant bodies — `retainedBody` decides HOW MUCH text crosses the boundary, never WHETHER that text is a credential. **log**: apps/web/src/lib/commands/bus.ts:298 does `console.error("[command] ${command.action} failed:", err)` on an arbitrary handler error whose command payload is caller-supplied, and apps/web/src/lib/ai.ts:139-146 logs 500 chars of a provider response body; nothing scans either. **config**: packages/configuration has a `sensitivity` LABEL (`definition.ts:14` lists `"secret"`) but no value-level refusal anywhere — `grep -n secret packages/configuration/src/*.ts` returns that constant and a sort order and nothing else, so a `sk_live_…` written into a ConfigValue is stored and later resolved into the snapshot the chat route reads. **evidence**: the ledger/registry evidence strings are prose nobody scans. And the guard file the prior survey named, tests/security/no-reusable-secrets-outside-the-vault.test.mjs, does not exist.
smallest_real_change: Give three of the four unguarded sinks the SAME implementation the outbox already uses, so there is one rule and four callers rather than four copies. (a) model: in `aiComplete` (ai.ts:101), run `findSecretValues` over `{ system, user }` before the fetch and return null with a named refusal rather than posting — this is the one boundary that leaves the account. (b) log: replace the two bare `console.error(..., err)` sites (bus.ts:298, ai.ts:139/146) with a `redactSecretValues`-wrapped message from @tenure/audit. (c) config: call `findSecretValues` in the configuration publication path and refuse the publish, mirroring `ProviderPayloadRefused` — a config value is exactly the "pasted into a note field" case secret-values.ts:5-8 was written about. Then add tests/security/no-reusable-secrets-outside-the-vault.test.mjs that (i) asserts each of the six sinks names a call site (a list of file+symbol pairs it resolves in source, so deleting a guard reds), and (ii) scans docs/implementation/*.md and docs/architecture/capability-completeness-registry.yaml for the `PATTERNS` in secret-values.ts:43-54, covering the evidence sink. Mutation for each: put `whsec_aaaaaaaaaa` into the prompt / the log payload / a config value and confirm the PRODUCTION path refuses — not `findSecretValues` called directly, which would stay green the day a caller stops using it.

title: The relay's only brake on a writing tool is `typeof confirmationToken === "string" && length > 0` — nothing mints it, nothing binds it to the proposal, nothing verifies it, and no relay invocation is audited at all
why_open: apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.ts:624-637 is the whole of the human-authority check: `if (tool.readOnly === false) { const token = proposal.args.confirmationToken; if (typeof token !== "string" || token.trim().length === 0) refuse }`. Any non-empty string passes, and the string comes from the same body the model's proposal comes from — so the model confirms itself. `grep -rn confirmationToken apps/web/src modules` finds it in exactly two places: that check and the unit test at relay-tools.test.ts:600-619, which passes the canned literal `"confirm_9f2"`. Nothing anywhere MINTS a confirmation, nothing binds one to a plan digest or to the arguments it approved, and nothing expires one — so the check is a shape assertion wearing the name of an authorization. Second half: nothing records that the relay ran. apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:245 calls `invokeRelayTool`, loads the caller's entire corpus at :270, and posts it to a vendor at :346 — and `grep -n recordAuditEvent apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts` returns nothing. Three comment hits about auditing, zero writes. An assistant that reads a tenant's whole corpus and leaves no attributable record of who asked, which tool was invoked, what risk class it carried and which sources were projected is precisely the "autonomous authority" this gate exists to refuse; today the only surviving evidence of a relay call is a CloudWatch line.
smallest_real_change: Two things, both in files this domain already owns. (1) Make the confirmation a real one: add `mintConfirmation(proposal, context)` / `verifyConfirmation(token, proposal, context, now)` beside `invokeRelayTool` — an HMAC over the tenant, actor, toolKey and a canonical digest of the non-caller-decided args, with a short expiry — and change the readOnly===false branch from a shape check to `verifyConfirmation`. A token minted for a different proposal, a different actor, or an expired one must refuse. This makes the existing `PROPOSAL_NOT_ACCEPTED { rejected: "confirmationToken" }` refusal mean what its name says. (2) Record the invocation: call `recordAuditEvent` (from @/lib/audit-record — NOT raw `db.auditEvent.create`, which is ratcheted at 32 in tests/security/audit-writes.test.mjs and may only fall) once per relay request with the toolKey, the riskClass `riskOf` returned, the activation verdict, and the source ids/kinds projected — never the bodies. Prove (1) by mutating the HMAC input to drop `toolKey` and asserting a token minted for `search.corpus` is rejected for `approvals.raise`; prove (2) through the ROUTE, asserting the row lands via the chat handler (and remember a jest mock of @/lib/db must implement BOTH the array and callback forms of `$transaction`, re-stated inside `beforeEach`, or `recordAuditEvent` silently writes nothing).

title: The outbox half of this requirement landed; the calendar half did not — `Event.recurrenceRule` is a column nothing writes, nothing reads and no feed emits, so "recurrence" cannot be tested because recurrence does not exist
why_open: The ledger still marks WRK-060-005 open and it is half wrong: duplicates, out-of-order, gaps, partial batches, Unicode, large payloads and stale conditional writes are now all covered against real Postgres by apps/web/src/lib/jobs/outbox-dispatch.itest.ts (describes at :160, :177, :215, :240, :269, :300-346) and `dispatchOnce` has a genuine production caller at apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/outbox/route.ts:90. What is untouched is recurrence. `apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma:617` declares `recurrenceRule String? // RFC 5545 RRULE`, and a repository-wide grep for `recurrenceRule` returns exactly two hits — that line and the baseline migration at apps/web/prisma/migrations/20260730000000_baseline/migration.sql:304. No writer sets it, no reader expands it, and `eventsToICS` (apps/web/src/lib/calendar-sync.ts:84-108) emits `BEGIN:VEVENT / DTSTART / DTEND / SUMMARY / …` with no `RRULE` line at all — so a weekly club meeting subscribed into Google or Outlook appears exactly once. `loadScopedEvents` (apps/web/src/lib/calendar-data.ts:45) returns raw rows, so the month and week grids have the same hole. The adjacent time-zone gap is the same shape: `Event.timezone` exists at schema.prisma:612 with a default, and `grep -rn timezone apps/web/src` shows every reader uses the INSTITUTION timezone (institution-time.ts) — the per-event column is never read, so an event in another timezone renders in the institution's.
smallest_real_change: Add one kernel-free module, `apps/web/src/lib/calendar-recurrence.ts`, that parses the RFC 5545 subset the column promises (FREQ=DAILY|WEEKLY|MONTHLY, INTERVAL, COUNT, UNTIL, BYDAY) and expands a stored event into occurrences within a window, resolved in the institution timezone via institution-time.ts so a DST boundary does not shift a 6pm meeting to 5pm. Then give it two production callers so it is not a declaration: (a) `eventsToICS` emits the `RRULE:` line verbatim for a recurring event (which is what an ICS consumer wants — one VEVENT plus a rule, not N copies), and (b) `loadScopedEvents` expands occurrences inside the requested range so the grid shows them. Keep the module free of manifoldless imports of @/lib/db so its unit test can import it directly. Prove with a table-driven test over DST-crossing weekly rules and a `COUNT`/`UNTIL` pair, plus one e2e that subscribes to the ICS feed and asserts an `RRULE:` line is present; mutation — drop `BYDAY` from the parser and confirm the DST test reds. Do not weaken the existing outbox itests; they already satisfy the rest of this requirement's list.

title: The whole external-identity linking engine — `planLink`, `planUnlink`, `validateMergeProposal`, `applyMerge`, `identityKey`, `proposalFromClaims` — has zero production callers; the real linking path is `PrismaAdapter(db)` and it never consults any of them
why_open: packages/identity carries a complete, well-argued linking design: `planLink` (linking.ts:126) refuses a collision instead of guessing, `planUnlink` (:219) refuses to remove the last way in, `validateMergeProposal`/`applyMerge` (:294/:388) make a merge a reviewed flow, `identityKey` (keying.ts:74) keys on connection+issuer+subject with a NUL separator, and `proposalFromClaims` (claims-input.ts:80) refuses email as the subject claim. `grep -rn 'planLink|identityKey|proposalFromClaims|applyMerge|validateMergeProposal'` across apps/ packages/ tests/ finds them ONLY inside packages/identity/src and inside two lexical guards (tests/security/email-is-not-a-key.test.mjs:166, claims-are-not-authority.test.mjs:138) that read the source as TEXT. No runtime path calls any of them. What actually links a credential to a person is apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:159 — `adapter: PrismaAdapter(db)` — with the Okta provider registered at :167-171; the adapter writes an `Account` row (apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma:19-36, unique on `[provider, providerAccountId]`) with no collision plan, no step-up freshness check, no last-way-in refusal, and no review when two people arrive at one credential. `apps/web` already imports @tenure/identity (auth.ts:8-13 takes `checkSession`), so this is a declaration that was never wired, not a missing dependency.
smallest_real_change: Wire the engine to the one linking path that exists, with no schema change: the `Account` row IS an `ExternalIdentity` under a different name — `provider`→connectionId, `providerAccountId`→subject, `OKTA_ISSUER`→issuer. Add a NextAuth `signIn` callback in apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts that (1) builds the assertion through `proposalFromClaims` with `subjectClaim: "sub"`, so email can never become the key, (2) computes `identityKey` and looks for an existing `Account` on `[provider, providerAccountId]`, (3) when the key is unknown but a User with that email already exists, runs `planLink` and REFUSES on `COLLISION` — returning false so NextAuth surfaces the generic `SIGN_IN_FAILED_MESSAGE` rather than silently attaching a second credential to somebody's account. That converts a real, reachable behaviour (an Okta account arriving for an address that already has a dev-login user) from "whatever the adapter does" into the reviewed refusal the Bible asks for. Prove it against the running database with an itest under apps/web/src/lib: seed a User plus an Account, replay an assertion with the same email and a DIFFERENT `sub`, assert no second Account row is written and the callback refused; mutation — return true unconditionally from the callback and confirm the itest reds. `npm run test:isolation` covers this path, so run it.

title: Nothing publishes the capability matrix — the honest PLANNED/AVAILABLE state lives only in TypeScript and a Studio page this run may not touch, so no reader outside the codebase can see what is supported or what is blocking it
why_open: The DATA is now honest and that is genuine progress: packages/provisioning/src/provider-packs.ts declares 24 packs (`microsoft.outlook-mail`:131 … `sharefile.content`:369), each `PLANNED` with `requirementIds` bound to real registry ids, and packages/provisioning/src/connector-capability.ts:125-158 refuses an `AVAILABLE`/`DEGRADED` claim that cites no evidence or disagrees with the artifact gate. But the requirement is to PUBLISH an exact matrix plus every limitation and external blocker, and nothing does. The only renderer is apps/system-studio/src/app/page.tsx:87 (`availabilityDecisions(CATALOG_ENTRIES, …)`) — an operator console, and a file this run is explicitly forbidden to touch. There is no matrix under docs/: `grep -rln 'capability matrix' docs README.md` returns only the registry, this ledger and two other ledgers — i.e. the requirement text quoting itself. So the external blockers (no Slack app credential, no Anthropic provider review — packages/platform-config/src/provider-review.ts:207) exist in code comments and nowhere a reader can find them, and there is no guard that would catch a future pack advancing past its evidence in a published claim.
smallest_real_change: Write docs/architecture/connector-capability-matrix.md as a generated artifact — one row per `provider/product/capability/direction` from PROVIDER_PACKS plus the Anthropic relay capability, each with its seven-state status, its `requirementIds`, its evidence refs, and a named external blocker for every non-PLANNED-able row — and add tests/architecture/capability-matrix-matches-catalog.test.mjs that parses BOTH the doc and provider-packs.ts (the same text-parsing technique provider-packs-bind-requirements.test.mjs already uses, because the platform test runner has no TypeScript loader) and fails when they disagree in either direction: a doc row for a pack that does not exist, a pack with no doc row, or a status that differs. That makes the matrix a published claim a machine re-checks rather than prose that rots. Mutation: flip one pack's lifecycle in provider-packs.ts and confirm the new test reds without the doc being touched. Stay out of apps/system-studio and packages/contracts.

title: The connector surfaces are the one part of the app outside every accessibility matrix — `MissingConnectionCard` and the settings connections list appear in no a11y spec, and neither is in the measured-journey scorecard
why_open: The generic matrices are real and strong: apps/web/e2e/a11y.spec.ts covers bypass blocks (:53), reflow at 320px (:80), target size (:135), focus not obscured (:161), focus visible (:205), no keyboard trap (:243), heading structure (:267), resize text (:310), status messages (:323), dragging (:352) and reduced motion (:430); localization.spec.ts:62-74 covers RTL; the four themes including `prefers-contrast: more` are covered by apps/web/src/lib/a11y/contrast.test.ts:104. None of them visits a connector surface. `grep -rln 'missing-connection|connection-outcome' apps/web/e2e` returns only relay.spec.ts, and the settings connections section is in no a11y spec at all — so the card that carries the ONE control a person gets when a capability is missing (MissingConnectionCard.tsx:66-88, an `ask-admin` or `connect` button plus a `Kept for when this connects:` region at :59) has never been checked for an accessible name, focus order, or announcement of the outcome change. It is also absent from docs/architecture/ux-task-scorecard.md — the persona table at :72-75 has four journeys, none of them a connection task — so WRK-GATE-110's "fast" and "non-fatiguing" have no number for the connector path even as an unmeasured `—` row.
smallest_real_change: Extend the existing matrices rather than starting a new suite. In a11y.spec.ts add a connector block that opens /settings, tabs to the connections list and the Relay panel's MissingConnectionCard, and asserts: every rendered control has a non-empty accessible name; the card's outcome change is announced (the `data-connection-outcome` attribute already exists as the hook); the card survives 320 CSS px reflow; and the `Kept for when this connects:` region is reachable in reading order. Add one row to the persona table in docs/architecture/ux-task-scorecard.md — `J05-connect-a-capability`, persona OSE director, "From the dashboard, find out why the assistant is unavailable and who can fix it" — with `—` budgets, since journey-metrics.ts refuses a MISSING row outright but tolerates an unmeasured one, and a corresponding journey in journeys.spec.ts driving real trusted clicks (never `locator.fill()`). Prove the a11y additions by removing the `aria-label` at MissingConnectionCard.tsx:70 and confirming the new spec reds. This item is smaller than the others and pairs naturally with WRK-030-005, which edits the same two surfaces.
